name: Bus Analysis & Protocol Sniffing
description: Interception, decoding, and analysis of communication protocols on PCB-level buses. Covers SPI, I2C, UART, SDIO, eMMC, parallel buses, and proprietary protocols. Includes physical tap installation, protocol decoding, traffic analysis, replay attacks, and man-in-the-middle interception for data extraction and command injection.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to hardware bus analysis or protocol sniffing

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands common embedded bus protocols and their security properties
evidence: Can describe common embedded protocols (SPI, I2C, UART, SDIO) and their signal characteristics
Understands the security implications of unencrypted bus communication
Aware of bus sniffing tools (Saleae, Bus Pirate, Glasgow Interface Explorer)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Captures and decodes standard bus protocols under supervision
evidence: Attaches probes to identified bus signals on a target PCB
Captures and decodes SPI, I2C, and UART traffic using a logic analyzer
Identifies command/response patterns in captured bus traffic with guidance
Performs basic replay of captured commands using a bus interface tool

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently analyzes bus protocols and performs active interception on real targets
evidence: Identifies and taps bus signals on unfamiliar PCBs without documentation
Decodes complex and multi-wire protocols (eMMC, parallel flash) independently
Performs man-in-the-middle interception to modify bus traffic in real-time
Extracts sensitive data (keys, credentials, firmware) from bus communications
Completed bus analysis on 3+ engagements with documented protocol findings

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Analyzes proprietary protocols; develops custom interception hardware; mentors team
evidence: Reverse engineers undocumented or proprietary bus protocols from signal analysis
Develops custom FPGA-based bus interception and injection hardware
Analyzes high-speed buses (PCIe, USB 3.x at PHY level) with appropriate tooling
Mentors team on protocol identification, tap installation, and traffic analysis techniques

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on hardware bus security; publishes research; defines methodology
evidence: Published research on bus-level attacks or protocol vulnerabilities
Defines the lab's bus analysis methodology and tool standards
Designs custom bus interception platforms used by the lab
Provides expert consultation on bus-level security to hardware designers

assessment_methods.description: Identify, tap, and decode bus communications on a prepared target device, then demonstrate data extraction or command injection
Observe probe attachment technique, protocol identification, and traffic analysis during a live bus sniffing session

equipment: Glasgow Interface Explorer or equivalent FPGA-based protocol analyzer
Bus Pirate or Tigard multi-protocol interface
